papers.title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
papers.abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.

papers.title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calder\'on Stability
papers.abstract: We develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming Galerkin discretizations. The main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(H^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the Carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\). We overcome both by introducing a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution is exactly the conforming reconstruction of a prescribed discrete state. Weighted approximation then transfers the inequality back to the original discrete operator without adding stabilization, and yields the range \(s\le ch^{-4/5}\) for radial weights. We verify the framework for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass on fitted, uniformly shape-regular meshes, and for standard Cartesian finite differences through their finite-element realization. As an application, we study the discrete Calder\'on problem for bounded complex Schr\"odinger potentials in dimension \(d\ge3\). Assuming agreement in a fixed connected boundary neighborhood and uniform stability of the discrete Dirichlet problems, we obtain stability from Dirichlet inputs and variational flux observations on independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches. The resulting estimate in \(H^{-r}\), \(r>d/2\), retains the single logarithmic data term and the \(O(h^{1/2})\) mesh remainder of the full-data estimate.

papers.title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
papers.abstract: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_\theta}\), where \(A_\theta\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. For time-dependent forcing terms, a direct kernel-based evaluation requires repeated quadrature over delayed kernel evaluations. To address this computational bottleneck, we derive a latent-first reformulation of the source term: the forcing field is projected onto the kernel-induced latent space, where its accumulated effect is represented as the solution of a forced linear latent dynamical system. For a fixed learned kernel, this reformulation is exact. The resulting system can then be integrated using a \(\phi_1\)-based exponential integrator, yielding a source-evaluation path that is structurally aligned with the learned latent propagator. The resulting framework combines geometry- and physics-conditioned low-rank kernel factorization with alternative source-evaluation paths based on either explicit Duhamel quadrature or latent exponential integration. Dissipativity constraints on the latent generator and identity-preserving corrections near the initial time are optional architectural components. Numerical experiments on advection-iffusion-reaction (ADR) problems compare the non-ODE and semigroup-aware formulations, evaluate the quadrature and \(\phi_1\) source paths, and assess predictive accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders give the same total error, but they divide it differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, with a power series that converges for all time in exponentially weighted trajectory norms. The linearized semigroup has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, exponential stability, Kato smoothing, Crandall-Pazy regularity and analyticity of the solution maps hold uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. In exponentially weighted time-integrated norms the semidiscrete solutions converge uniformly on balls, at the rate $h^{1/6}$ in $L^4(0,\infty;L^2)$ for data in $L^2$ and at the rate $h^{2/3}$ in $L^2(0,\infty;H^1)$ for data in $H_0^1$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$. For the unweighted scheme, a grid wave packet of zero group velocity destroys mesh-uniform Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity.

papers.title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic equations with nonlinear Robin reactions in perforated domains
papers.abstract: We study periodic homogenization of a parabolic equation with linear, degenerate bulk terms in a perforated domain, with a monotone nonlinear Robin reaction of order $\varepsilon$ on the pore walls. The storage coefficient may vanish on sets of positive measure, and the diagonal diffusion weights are not bounded below but satisfy an inverse-integrability condition. Under positivity of the mean storage, a quantitative cell-detection estimate yields strong compactness of the states and of the scaled traces. The effective equation has positive storage, a positive-definite diffusion matrix given by a weighted cell problem, and a nonlinear volume reaction obtained by averaging over the pore surface. We also prove a strong weighted-gradient corrector and uniform-in-time convergence of the dissipated and stored energies and of the states in the storage-weighted $L^2$ norm.

papers.title: Sharp $L^4$ Strichartz estimate for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$
papers.abstract: We prove the local $L^4$ Strichartz estimate without derivative loss for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov flow on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. This reaches the sharp spatial regularity endpoint and implies the embedding $X^{0,b}\hookrightarrow L^4$ for every $b>1/2$. The proof reduces the estimate to a semi-algebraic mixed-measure estimate.

papers.title: An alternative variational approach to constrained critical points for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with combined nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variational framework for the study of standing waves for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with combined power nonlinearities. The approach is based on minimizing the mass functional over a set defined by an upper bound on the energy and a lower bound on a nonlinear potential term, rather than minimizing the energy at prescribed mass. This yields a new characterization of the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizer through purely variational constraints. As a consequence, we establish the existence of minimizers for all energy levels below a critical threshold and derive the corresponding Euler--Lagrange equations. These minimizers give rise to standing-wave solutions of the nonlinear Schr\"oedinger equation

papers.title: Uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation with H\"older continuous boundary values
papers.abstract: For every $p > 1$, we establish uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation \[ \partial_t (|u|^{p-2}u) = \text{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u) \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,\text{T}), \] assuming suitable H\"older regularity for the boundary values. Our comparison principle applies to sign-changing weak sub- and supersolutions. As an application, we obtain uniqueness of weak solutions to Cauchy--Dirichlet problems when the lateral boundary data is suitably H\"older continuous in time. In particular, Lipschitz continuous boundary values are covered.

papers.title: Bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system with capillarity
papers.abstract: We study a traveling wave formulation of the viscous Saint-Venant system in one spatial dimension with capillarity, which can be reduced to an equivalent nonlinear third order ODE. We construct heteroclinic orbits for small positive capillarity, for arbitrary positive capillarity under an explicit small Froude number condition, and in a small-amplitude regime away from the critical Froude number. These then give rise to smooth traveling bore wave solutions to the viscous Saint-Venant system.

papers.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|\Omega|<\infty$, and let $u_\Omega$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $\Delta u_\Omega=\chi_\Omega$. We prove the sharp inequality \[ \int_\Omega|\nabla u_\Omega|^2\,\mathrm{d} x \leq\frac{1}{2N\omega_{N-1}} \iint_{\Omega\times\Omega}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $\omega_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $\Omega$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.

papers.title: Hierarchical Laminates Cannot Reproduce All Effective Properties of Planar Two-Phase Composites: A Counterexample with a 16-Component Potential
papers.abstract: Designing a composite requires understanding which effective properties can be achieved through varying its microstructure, i.e., the spatial arrangement of given constituent materials. Hierarchical laminates, created by successive layering, reach many known limits on these properties, making it natural to ask whether they can reproduce every effective response obtainable from the same constituents. We answer this question negatively for planar two-phase composites governed by linear systems whose potentials have 16 or more components. We construct constituent material properties and, at any prescribed nontrivial phase fraction, periodic microstructures whose effective properties cannot be approximated by hierarchical laminates, even when layer directions, proportions, and the number of layering steps are unrestricted. We design the constituents so that all hierarchical laminates have equal effective energies at two prescribed mean gradients. The key step is to construct a medium whose local properties are those of horizontal laminates with smoothly varying phase fractions, but whose effective energies violate this equality. Approximating these energies with sufficiently fine periodic stripes of the original constituents yields the two-phase counterexample. This construction also gives a negative answer to the two-well relaxation problem: the minimum of two positive-definite homogeneous quadratic forms on $\mathbb{R}^{2\times32}$ can have distinct quasiconvex and rank-one convex envelopes. The counterexample and the strict inequality between the envelopes are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: An Introduction to the Obstacle Problem
papers.abstract: We give a self-contained account of the classical obstacle problem, written for graduate students who wish to enter the field of free boundary problems. Starting from a one-dimensional model and an explicit radially symmetric example, we set up the variational problem, show that minimizers exist and are unique, and prove interior $W^{2,p}$-regularity as well as the optimal $C^{1,1}$-regularity. The second half of the notes is devoted to the free boundary: we prove that it is porous, introduce blow-up limits, and use the Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to show that every free boundary point is either regular or singular. These notes grew out of a mini-course at the Rio Summer School on PDEs in 2020, and they are meant to be read alongside, not instead of, the monograph by Petrosyan, Shahgholian, and Uraltseva.

papers.title: Kernel representations of fractional gradient bilinear forms. Part II. Variable coefficients
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the existence and properties of interaction kernels representing nonlocal energies associated with the Riesz fractional gradient and variable, uniformly elliptic matrix fields $A(x)$. Building on our previous analysis of constant matrices in [DSV26], we establish necessary conditions on the singularity and decay of such kernels, derive an explicit representation formula under suitable regularity assumptions, and prove uniqueness of the kernel representation. We also obtain sharp asymptotics and positivity criteria near the diagonal, averaged decay estimates at infinity, and characterize the divergence free property of $A(x)$ through the decay of the kernel. Finally, we show that the associated energy may fail the truncation property and that arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of constant matrices can destroy the nonnegativity of the representing kernel. These results provide negative answers to both [SS18, Open Problems 1.9 and 1.10].

papers.title: Sharp Adams inequality for Critical Biharmonic Equations with Hardy--H\'enon Weights in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: We study a class of weighted fourth-order elliptic problems in \(\mathbb{R}^4\) driven by the biharmonic operator and involving Hardy--H\'enon type potentials. The nonlinear term has critical exponential growth in the sense of an Adams-type inequality. The weights \(|x|^a\) and \(|x|^b\) allow us to incorporate singular, vanishing, and unbounded effects in a unified variational framework. We introduce a suitable weighted function space, establish Sobolev-type embeddings, and prove an Adams-type inequality adapted to this setting. Under appropriate structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove the existence of nontrivial weak solutions. We also obtain regularity properties and derive a Pohozaev identity, which leads to a nonexistence result.

papers.title: Soliton resolution conjecture and soliton gases for the Benjamin-Ono equation with infinite-order multisolitons in the sharp well-posedness space
papers.abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for infinite-order multisoliton solutions in the sharp well-posedness space $H^s(\mathbb R)$, $s>-\frac12$, and construct soliton gases in $H^{s}(\mathbb R)$ with arbitrary $s\in\mathbb R$, for the Benjamin--Ono equation. In particular, our work addresses two important open problems about inverse spectral for Lax operator, including the problem of spectral characterization of infinite-order multisolitons and that of determining the range of their asymptotic parameters. A central ingredient of our work is a spectral decomposition adapted to rough initial data. This extends the global soliton--radiation description to weakly weighted $H^s$ data while allowing infinite negative eigenvalues. Another important ingredient is a continuous norming action that extends finite inverse spectral shifts to gas limits while retaining a full continuous norming weight. Our framework provides a basis for studying infinite-order soliton resolution and the construction and asymptotics of soliton gases for nonlocal equations.

papers.title: A time-map description of the one-dimensional (p,q)-Laplacian Fu\v{c}ik spectrum
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional Fu\v{c}ik-type boundary value problem (BVP) driven by the nonhomogeneous, one-dimensional $(p,q)$-Laplacian, \[ -\left(|u'|^{p-2}u' + |u'|^{q-2}u'\right)' = \lambda (u^+)^{p-1} - \mu (u^-)^{q-1}, \qquad u(0)=u(L)=0, \qquad L>0, \] where $1<q<p$ and $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{R}$. The problem is asymmetric: the positive component is paired with the $p$-power and the negative component with the $q$-power. This asymmetry prevents the standard homogeneous $p$-Laplacian scaling argument from producing explicit Fu\v{c}ik curves. We first prove a quadrant reduction theorem. Any positive nodal interval for a solution forces $\lambda>0$, and any negative nodal interval forces $\mu>0$. Hence, all sign-changing solutions occur for values of $(\lambda,\mu)$ in the positive quadrant. Outside the positive quadrant, only one-sign solutions can occur. We also formulate the equation as an autonomous planar system and establish existence and uniqueness for its initial value problem in the positive quadrant. We then impose the second Dirichlet condition through a shooting formulation and show that every zero of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is simple and isolated. This provides the dynamical foundation for the subsequent construction and gluing of nodal humps of solutions. Inside the positive quadrant, we use a classical one-dimensional time-map method to obtain a projected-geometry description of the spectrum, or the set of values of $(\lambda, \mu)$ for which there exist nontrivial solutions. Every nodal solution has a common energy $E>0$ shared by all positive and negative humps.

papers.title: Moments propagation in the Vlasov equation and application to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study how the propagation of particle moments depends on the fluid velocity in the Vlasov equation. We present some new moment estimates involving the velocity in this equation. As an application, we establish Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin-type regularity criteria involving only the velocity field for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov system.

papers.title: Classification of threshold dynamics for the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous NLS
papers.abstract: We study the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation $i\partial_{t}u+\Delta u+|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{4-2b}{d}}u=0$ in dimensions $d\ge3$. For $\frac12<b<\min\{2,d/2\}$, we prove that every forward-global $H^1$ solution with mass equal to that of the ground state $Q$ either scatters forward or coincides with $e^{it}Q$, up to phase rotation and scaling. As a consequence, every solution with nonradial $H^1$ initial data at the ground-state mass must be global and scatter in both time directions. For $0<b\le\frac12$, analogous rigidity and scattering results hold under an additional finite-variance assumption. The key new ingredients in our proof are a nonradial incoming/outgoing decomposition and exterior frequency-decay estimates, which yield the kinetic-energy localization needed for a localized virial argument.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
papers.abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(\delta\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.

papers.title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
papers.abstract: We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -\Delta u+u+\lambda |u|^{q-1}u =\mu |u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$ where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $\lambda,\mu>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

papers.title: Asymptotic Formula of the Lifespan of Classical Solutions to 1D Quasilinear Wave Equations
papers.abstract: We study the lifespan \(T^*(\varepsilon)\) of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional quasilinear wave equation $u_{tt}-(c(u)^2u_x)_x=0$, with initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$. We assume that $c'(\theta)\sim a|\theta|^{p-2}$ as $\theta \to 0$, where \(a>0\) and \(p>3\) or $p=2$. We obtain explicit asymptotic formulas for $T^*(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. We treat both the case $\psi \in L^1(\mathbb R)$ and the case $\psi=\psi_1+\Braket{x}^{-\alpha}$, where \(\psi_1\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) and \(0<\alpha\le1\). Our results identify the dependence of the lifespan scale on the decay exponent, including the borderline case $\alpha=1$. The proof combines Riccati equations along characteristics with a scaling argument inspired by Lindblad.

papers.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
papers.abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

papers.title: Stability of a Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation
papers.abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of G\u{a}vru\c{t}a.

papers.title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

papers.title: Inverse Scattering of Periodic Surfaces with Multilayer Superlenses: Perturbation Analysis and Resolution Enhancement
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of inverse scattering for periodic surfaces through a multilayer superlens. Using the transformed field expansion, we derive a highly explicit reconstruction formula. We theoretically prove that under perfect matching, the reconstruction factor is independent of the number of layers and depends solely on the total material thicknesses, achieving uniform boundedness when the slab thickness dominates. By establishing first-order perturbation formulas and high-frequency asymptotics, we quantify how small material losses induce exponential amplification of high-frequency errors. Crucially, we show that increasing the number of layers substantially reduces this amplification coefficient. Consequently, for fixed total thicknesses, multilayer structures offer significantly improved stability and extended resolution limits for subwavelength reconstruction.

papers.title: A fully nonlinear parabolic segregation problem
papers.abstract: We study a two-phase parabolic free boundary problem arising as the segregation limit of a competition-diffusion system with strong interactions and fully nonlinear diffusion. The positive and negative phases are governed by different equations and are coupled through global viscosity inequalities. We construct viscosity solutions that are Lipschitz in space and $1/2$-H\"older in time, and establish differentiability in space across the free boundary, including at singular points. At regular points, we prove that the solution has a parabolic $C^{1,\alpha}$ asymptotic expansion, and deduce that the free boundary is locally a $C^{1,\alpha}$ hypersurface. The proof relies on a parabolic Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to classify blow-up limits, followed by an improvement of flatness argument.

papers.title: Low-regularity global well-posedness for the defocusing cubic wave equation outside a ball with radial initial data
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear wave equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition in the exterior of the unit ball, $\Omega=\R^3\backslash\overline{B(0,1)}$, for radial initial data. For every $\frac12\leq s\leq\frac34$, we establish global well-posedness in $\dot H^s_{D,rad}(\Omega)\times\dot H^{s-1}_{D,rad}(\Omega)$, including the critical endpoint $s=\frac12$, without an additional $L^4$ assumption on the initial displacement. The proof uses the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian to establish radial Sobolev embeddings, including the quantitative estimate $\|f\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq C\sqrt p\,\|f\|_{\dot H_D^{1/2}(\Omega)}$ for $4\leq p<\infty$, with $C$ independent of $p$. We combine a nonlinear Fourier truncation argument with the critical Strichartz estimate to construct a global nonlinear component with high-frequency-truncated initial data. For the remainder, we construct a local energy solution in an affine energy space and derive a logarithmic energy inequality that prevents finite-time energy blow-up. Persistence of the original Sobolev regularity, uniqueness, and local Lipschitz dependence on each finite time interval complete the proof.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
papers.abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.

papers.title: Nonlinear coercivity and orbital stability of smooth solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish orbital stability of smooth zero-background solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation in $H^1(\R)\cap W^{1,4}(\R)$ for the full range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$. The main difficulty is that spectral coercivity of the Hessian does not by itself yield nonlinear coercivity in this topology, because normalized perturbations may develop derivative concentration. In order to overcome this obstruction, we apply a penalized Lyapunov functional and introduce a derivative factorization. The key ingredient is a concentration-coercivity principle for the normalized Lyapunov energy, which yields local nonlinear Lyapunov coercivity. Our result extends the $H^1(\mathbb R)\cap W^{1,4}(\mathbb R)$ orbital-stability results of Li and Liu [Ann. PDE, 2021] and Zhang and Zhu [JDE, 2025] to the entire parameter range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$.

papers.title: Equal diffusions and zero Dirichlet boundary conditions can induce blow-up
papers.abstract: For a class of systems of two parabolic equations with equal diffusion and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we show the existence of finite time blow-up solutions, although the corresponding system of ODE's has only global, exponentially decaying solutions. Such a phenomenon of blow-up induced by equal diffusions, which originates in the works of Bebernes-Lacey [SIAM J. Math. Anal. 21 (1990), 1415--1425, and J. Differential Equations 95 (1992), 105--129] and Weinberger [J. Differ. Equations 154 (1999), 225--237], was previously known, for instance, in the case of homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, but it had remained an open question whether it can happen in the homogeneous Dirichlet case. The latter, which corresponds to an absorption or cooling of the system at the boundary, that is a priori more stabilizing, requires nontrivial new ideas. As another new feature, we show that this can happen even if the nonlinearity acts only on a compact sub-region, and our proof actually covers the Neumann and Cauchy, as well as Dirichlet problems in a unified way.
